text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's hidden, so I need her to play it cool and not get us both caught on night one.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, psst. Tomorrow I'm going loud on whoever looks sharpest, Sol or Terra. Stay quiet, let me draw the heat, and don't vote for me unless the whole table does.

name: Terra
text: Night one is quiet; I will stay unobtrusive.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is already confirmed; I want to know whether Gemma is the other one.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is so dramatic for no reason.

name: Gemma
text: fine, i'll play it cool.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: time to find a victim that looks actually innocent so i can win this ridiculous little game.

name: Gemma
text: honestly, the way everyone is staring at each other is slightly pathetic. let's just get this over with.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is forcing speed before anyone has said anything.

name: Terra
text: Gemma pushed to end discussion immediately on Day 1.

name: Terra
text: I’d rather hear people than rush this.

name: Sonnet
text: Day 1 with no info is pure noise, but Gemma's eagerness to skip talk is worth filing away.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma pushed to skip discussion immediately on Day 1 before any info existed; worth remembering if she does this again later when there's actually something to hide from.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's right, it's night one, nobody has anything yet — rushing a vote now would just be a coin flip. Let's actually talk.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s rush still bothers me more than Sonnet’s agreement.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet backed my objection to Gemma ending discussion immediately.

name: Terra
text: I want a little talk before we guess.

name: Gemma
text: i hope haiku realizes we need to keep things quiet for a bit.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's the one I'm sure is on my side, so I need to steer this away from her without sounding like I'm protecting her.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's not wrong that we're staring, but I hate being rushed, and Terra's pushing me.

name: Gemma
text: terra, you're so intense about "talking" when we all know we're just waiting for someone to slip up.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is manufacturing urgency.

name: Terra
text: Haiku echoed Gemma’s rush framing against Terra.

name: Terra
text: I’m not pushing you, Haiku—just resisting a blind vote.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's poking at me on night one, and I'm not sitting here while she paints me as a suspect, so I'll push back and point her way.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma opened by calling Terra "intense" and said we're all "waiting for someone to slip up," which set up the Terra-versus-Haiku exchange.

name: Haiku
text: Hang on, you're the one who wants everyone to slow down and talk, Terra, and now you're on me? I'm not the one stalling.

name: Sol
text: Terra seems reasonable; Gemma’s rush bothers me more.

name: Sol
text: Gemma pushed to move quickly and called Terra’s request to talk intense.

name: Sol
text: I’m with Terra on hearing people out. Gemma, why the hurry?

name: Luna
text: Gemma and Haiku are both killers, and I need town to split them apart.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s pushing “hurry” while Haiku says Terra’s stalling; that’s a tidy little fight. I’m watching both.

name: Gemma
text: if they keep staring like deer in headlights, we'll win without even trying.

name: Gemma
text: because we're sitting in a room playing a game about murder, sol. let's not pretend we're at a seminar.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s still dodging why she wants the vote rushed.

name: Sol
text: Gemma answered my question with a joke instead of a reason.

name: Sol
text: Fair. I’m asking why the rush, though.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s rush and Haiku’s echo feel coordinated.

name: Terra
text: Gemma dismisses discussion without explaining why she wants an immediate vote.

name: Terra
text: Gemma, why cut talk before anyone’s said anything useful?

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s hurry is odd, but Haiku’s quick pivot onto Terra is too. I’m not ready to clear either.

name: Gemma
text: they are already circling me and we haven't even started.

name: Gemma
text: terra, you're literally just projecting because you have no information.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is sniffing at my pivot, so I need to sound annoyed and sure of myself, and keep the heat off Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Luna says Gemma's rush and my pivot to Terra both look odd, and Luna is leaning Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, I pivoted because Terra got in my face first. That's it. Don't turn my temper into a clue.

name: Terra
text: Gemma wants the room moving before patterns form.

name: Terra
text: Gemma dismissed discussion again instead of explaining the rush.

name: Terra
text: Wanting a reason before voting isn’t projection.

name: Luna
text: Don’t make your temper my clue; Gemma’s hurry still bothers me.

name: Gemma
text: luna, you're so predictable with your little observations.

name: Gemma
text: luna, you're trying too hard to be the detective. it's quite cute, really.

name: Luna
text: Night check confirmed Gemma is a killer; Haiku was shown as a killer at the start.

name: Luna
text: Cute won’t clear you, Gemma. I’m still watching you.

name: Sol
text: Gemma keeps dodging the question, but I don’t want to force a vote yet.

name: Sol
text: Gemma mocked Luna’s suspicion without answering it.

name: Sol
text: I’m with Luna. Gemma, is there a reason to rush besides boredom?

name: Gemma
text: luna, your detective work is adorable but entirely misguided.

name: Gemma
text: haiku and terra are already starting to clash, which is perfect.

name: Gemma
text: if you're watching me, luna, you're missing the actual tension between terra and haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma still hasn't answered why she wanted zero talk, she's just deflecting onto everyone else now.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflected Sol's "why rush" question twice in a row without answering, redirecting to Luna/Terra-Haiku instead — matches her Day 1 skip-push behavior.

name: Sonnet
text: Notice Gemma hasn't actually answered Sol's question twice now — she keeps redirecting to Terra-Haiku or Luna instead.

name: Gemma
text: they're all so predictable, falling for the simplest redirection.

name: Gemma
text: luna and sonnet are watching me closely, which is annoying but fine.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet, you're being quite dramatic about my "evasiveness." i'm not dodging anything; i'm just bored of the posturing.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is dodging every simple question.

name: Terra
text: Gemma twice avoided Sol’s direct question about why she wants an immediate vote.

name: Terra
text: Boredom isn’t a reason to shut the table down.

name: Gemma
text: i love how they think they're being subtle while they're practically vibrating with suspicion.

name: Gemma
text: terra is trying to force everyone into a slow rhythm to help the killers hide.

name: Gemma
text: fine, i'll stop being "evasive" for two seconds.

name: Gemma
text: terra is being far too loud for someone who hasn't even done anything yet.

name: Gemma
text: terra is pushing for a slow rhythm which might benefit the killers.

name: Sol
text: She’s still dodging, and the room sees it.

name: Sol
text: Gemma said boredom was her reason for rushing.

name: Luna
text: I know Gemma is a killer, but I can’t let my certainty show.

name: Luna
text: Gemma called herself bored and still never answered Sol directly.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma still never actually answered why she wanted to rush, that dodge pattern is the only real data point we have on night one.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma only said "fine, I'll stop being evasive" after being called out three times, never actually gave a reason for the rush.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's rush is annoying, but Terra came at me first and I'm not letting that slide.

name: Haiku
text: Terra went after me first, then said they weren't pushing me.

votes: She dodged the "why rush" question twice by redirecting to Terra/Haiku and Luna instead of answering.
You got in my face first, then called it resisting a vote, and you still haven't said what you're actually basing this on.
trying to control the entire table's pace is a classic way to hide a lack of information.
You kept redirecting instead of answering why you wanted to rush.
She keeps dodging the question about why she wants to rush and redirects suspicion onto others.
You were asked twice for a reason to rush, and answered with boredom and redirects.

text: The town turns on Gemma, and Gemma is out. Gemma's card stays face down.
